# Public Tally exchange fixtures

These are synthetic test books assembled from documented Tally XML structures. They contain fabricated identities and references. They are not exports from a private company or a running Tally installation.

The invoice uses the public invoice example's arithmetic, comprising party debit 21,546, sales credits 15,000 and 3,000, packing credit 900 and tax credit 2,646. Additional test records cover opening paise, a custom payment type, cancelled and optional entries, an order, inventory allocations, bank references, costs and an extension field.

Official references checked on 08-11-2026 are [Tally sample XML](https://help.tallysolutions.com/sample-xml/), [master and voucher exports](https://help.tallysolutions.com/how-to-export-import-entire-data-masters-transactions-to-a-new-company/), [native JSON](https://help.tallysolutions.com/tally-prime-integration-using-json-1/), [optional vouchers](https://help.tallysolutions.com/create-optional-voucher/), and [sales order accounting treatment](https://help.tallysolutions.com/article/Tally.ERP9/sales/sales-order-tally.htm).

Tests prove the import projection, preservation and reconciliation against these fixtures. Runtime equivalence with a licensed Tally installation requires exported books and corresponding Tally reports from that installation.

The publisher's integration demo ZIP and the invoice-mode envelope from TallyHelp are fetched locally into `official/` by `python3 tools/prepare-resources.py --fetch --tests`. They are excluded from the public source checkout. See [official fixture provenance](official/README.md) for the pinned source URLs, hashes and XML normalization. Voucher dates, numbers, accounting amounts, flags and inventory allocations keep the published values. The ZIP remains verbatim; the verifier reads one payment request and its response from it.

After resource setup, run `node tools/verify-tally-public-examples.mjs` from the project. It supplies six prerequisite ledger masters, one simple unit and two synthetic stock masters for the demonstration requests, checks strict conflict detection and operator-selected sign handling, and uses the ordinary HTTP preview, create, backup and restore routes. The synthetic stock opening is two units of each published item, valued at ₹20,000 for the televisions and ₹4,000 for the DVD players. These invented prerequisite costs are labelled in the evidence and do not come from TallyHelp. The exact published invoice movements leave one of each item, with combined closing stock and cost of goods sold of ₹12,000 each under this synthetic basis. The verifier prints source hashes, ledger postings, bill references and stock results; generated verification output is not part of the public source checkout. Sources are [Tally integration demo files](https://help.tallysolutions.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Integration_Demo_Samples.zip) and [TallyHelp Sample XML](https://help.tallysolutions.com/sample-xml/).

`StockMasters.xml` and `StockVouchers.xml` are synthetic quantity/cost fixtures: ten widgets opening across Main Location and Workshop, a two-widget sale, a three-widget purchase and a four-widget location transfer. The expected closing quantity is eleven and closing value ₹950; the sale consumes ₹200 of cost despite its ₹500 selling amount. The XML shapes follow the public [stock object appendix](https://help.tallysolutions.com/developer-reference/tally-definition-language/appendix/) and [godown transfer instructions](https://help.tallysolutions.com/inventory-and-manufacturing-faq/). No live Tally export or import was used for those synthetic transfers.
